title: Transition to Reality: Application of the Palace to the World and Statement of the Two Parties

questions.question: What does the palace stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for this world.

questions.question: In this comparison, what do the roof and floor of the palace represent?
questions.answer: The roof represents the sky, and the floor represents the earth.

questions.question: Who is the king in the comparison?
questions.answer: The king represents Allah, the holy and everlasting ruler.

questions.question: What shows the king’s great power in the passage?
questions.answer: He created the heavens and the earth and controls the sun, moon, and stars.

questions.question: What do the many rooms of the palace represent?
questions.answer: They represent the many different worlds or realms that are arranged in their own proper way.

questions.question: What do the amazing arts in the palace point to in the real meaning?
questions.answer: They point to Allah’s powerful works and wonders in the world.

questions.question: What do the foods in the palace point to?
questions.answer: They point to the blessings and fruits of Allah’s mercy, especially the fruits of summer.

questions.question: What does the stove and kitchen of the palace represent?
questions.answer: It represents the earth, which has fire inside it and produces things on its surface.

questions.question: What do the jewels from hidden treasures represent?
questions.answer: They represent signs of Allah’s beautiful names.

questions.question: What do the fine patterns and decorations represent?
questions.answer: They represent the orderly created beings in the world that show Allah’s power and names.

questions.question: Who does the master represent?
questions.answer: He represents Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Who are the master’s helpers in the comparison?
questions.answer: They are the prophets, peace be upon them.

questions.question: Who do the ruler’s servants in the palace represent?
questions.answer: They represent the angels.

questions.question: Who are the guests invited to the banquet in the real meaning?
questions.answer: They are jinn, human beings, and animals.

questions.question: How are animals described in relation to human beings here?
questions.answer: They are described as serving human beings.

questions.question: Who are the first of the two groups in the world?
questions.answer: They are the people of faith, who follow the Qur’an.

questions.question: Who are the second group?
questions.answer: They are the people of unbelief and rebellion.

questions.question: What causes the second group to go astray?
questions.answer: They follow Satan and their selfish lower desires.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the spiritual condition of the misguided group?
questions.answer: It says they are like animals, or even lower, because they only care about worldly life.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this passage after the story ends?
questions.answer: It explains the real meaning behind the comparison.

questions.question: What is the “truth” that the reader is asked to look at?
questions.answer: It is the real meaning of the palace story and what each part stands for.

questions.question: What does the world look like in the comparison of the palace?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a great palace with the sky above and the earth below.

questions.question: How is the sky described in this comparison?
questions.answer: It is described as bright with stars.

questions.question: How is the earth described in this comparison?
questions.answer: It is described as decorated with many kinds of flowers.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah by calling Him the everlasting ruler?
questions.answer: It teaches that He existed before all things and remains forever.

questions.question: What do all things in the heavens and earth do for Allah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They glorify and praise Him in their own ways.

questions.question: What example of order in the universe is given in the passage?
questions.answer: The changing of night and day is given as a sign of His rule.

questions.question: What does it mean that the sun, moon, and stars are under His command?
questions.answer: It means they obey Allah and move by His will.

questions.question: What do the palace apartments teach us about creation?
questions.answer: They teach that different parts of creation are arranged with wisdom and care.

questions.question: If the palace arts represent divine power, what do we learn when we study nature?
questions.answer: We learn about Allah’s power and wisdom through what He created.

questions.question: Why are summer fruits mentioned especially?
questions.answer: Because they are clear examples of Allah’s mercy and provision.

questions.question: What does the mention of hidden treasures help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that creation shows precious meanings from Allah’s names.

questions.question: How do created things act like signs in this passage?
questions.answer: They point beyond themselves to their Maker.

questions.question: Why are angels compared to servants in the palace?
questions.answer: Because they carry out Allah’s commands in the world.

questions.question: Which beings are counted among the guests in this worldly guesthouse?
questions.answer: Jinn, humans, and animals.

questions.question: What makes the first group different from the second group?
questions.answer: The first group believes and follows the Qur’an, while the second group rejects truth and follows evil desires.

questions.question: What does the passage say the palace really is?
questions.answer: It is the world we live in.

questions.question: What two big parts of the world are compared to the roof and the floor of the palace?
questions.answer: The sky and the earth.

questions.question: Who is described as the ruler of this palace-like world?
questions.answer: Allah is the ruler.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying all things praise Him with their own tongues?
questions.answer: Everything in creation shows His greatness in its own way.

questions.question: What mighty act of creation is mentioned to show His power?
questions.answer: Creating the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What regular change in the world is mentioned as a sign from Allah?
questions.answer: The turning of night and day.

questions.question: What heavenly bodies are said to be under His command?
questions.answer: The sun, moon, and stars.

questions.question: What are the palace rooms compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to many different worlds or levels of creation.

questions.question: What do the unusual arts in the palace correspond to in real life?
questions.answer: They correspond to the amazing works of Allah’s power in the world.

questions.question: What do the foods in the comparison help us think about in the world?
questions.answer: They help us think about Allah’s blessings and provision.

questions.question: What part of the world is compared to the stove and kitchen?
questions.answer: The earth itself.

questions.question: Why might the earth be compared to a kitchen in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it produces many things and has fire within it.

questions.question: What do the jewels stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for reflections of Allah’s beautiful names.

questions.question: What do the patterns and decorations stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for created things that are made in a careful and beautiful way.

questions.question: Who is the teacher in the real meaning of the comparison?
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Who are his assistants?
questions.answer: The prophets, peace be upon them.

questions.question: Who are his students?
questions.answer: The saints and purified scholars.

questions.question: Who do the palace servants stand for?
questions.answer: The angels.

questions.question: Who are the guests in this world?
questions.answer: Jinn, humans, and animals.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the believing group?
questions.answer: They are people of faith who learn from the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the unbelieving group?
questions.answer: They are people who rebel, follow Satan and selfish desires, and care only for worldly life.

questions.question: What can we infer about the Qur’an from this passage?
questions.answer: It helps people understand the signs spread throughout the universe.

questions.question: After the story ends, what is the reader invited to understand?
questions.answer: The deeper meaning of the comparison.

questions.question: What two bad influences do they follow?
